html:
The Tsardom of Russia was the Russian state from 1547, when Ivan IV was crowned tsar, until 1721, when Peter the Great proclaimed the Russian Empire. The map shows it from 1530 to 1715, growing in every snapshot.

Ivan IV, the Terrible, conquered the khanates of Kazan in 1552 and Astrakhan in 1556, which gave Russia the whole Volga. He built Saint Basil's Cathedral to mark the first victory. Late in his reign the Cossack Yermak crossed the Urals, and within sixty years Russians reached the Pacific.

When the old dynasty died out, the Time of Troubles brought famine, pretenders and a Polish army in Moscow. In 1613 an assembly chose Michael Romanov as tsar, founding the Romanov dynasty. The law code of 1649 bound peasants to the land as serfs. Church reforms split off the Old Believers. Peter the Great turned the tsardom toward Europe and made it an empire, the next stage of Muscovy, Russia, USSR.
